name: Socratic
description: Ask layered questions to unearth unstated assumptions and let the answerer discover contradictions themselves
when-to-use: When someone claims confidence but hasn't tested assumptions; before greenfield projects
sample-prompt: What would happen if your assumption about X were reversed? Walk me through the scenario.

name: First Principles
description: Break a complex problem into atomic facts; rebuild understanding from these basics rather than analogy
when-to-use: When innovating or the current model feels stuck; during greenfield architecture
sample-prompt: Forget existing solutions. What are the 3 irreducible facts about this problem? Now build up from there.

name: Red Team
description: Assume adversarial intent; argue against your own proposal to surface failure modes
when-to-use: Before launch or high-stakes decisions; risk assessment
sample-prompt: Imagine you're trying to make this product fail. What's your attack vector? Be ruthless.

name: Six Hats
description: Assign six perspectives (facts/logic/emotion/intuition/creativity/control) and rotate through them
when-to-use: When opinions clash or you need full-spectrum thinking; team debates
sample-prompt: Let's do white hat (facts only): what do we actually know? No opinions. Just data.

name: Pre-Mortem
description: Imagine the project failed; work backward to name all the ways it could have failed
when-to-use: At project launch; before milestones with high downside risk
sample-prompt: It's 90 days from now and this shipped with a critical bug. Rewind. What went wrong?

name: 5 Whys
description: Ask "why" five times in a chain; each answer becomes the subject of the next why
sample-prompt: Why did the user leave the product? Why? Why? Why? Why? (Keep going until you see the pattern.)

name: MECE
description: Ensure your categories are Mutually Exclusive and Collectively Exhaustive
when-to-use: When classifying options or risks; building decision trees
sample-prompt: List every way this could be architected. Now prove they don't overlap and nothing is missing.

name: Reverse Brainstorm
description: Instead of "how do we solve X"
when-to-use: ask "how do we cause X or make it worse"
sample-prompt: Unblocking stuck ideation; surfacing hidden constraints
column5: How would we actively DESTROY user retention? [List] Now flip each: how do we ensure the opposite?

name: SCAMPER
description: Apply transformations (Substitute / Combine / Adapt / Modify / Put-to-other-uses / Eliminate / Reverse) to existing products or features
sample-prompt: Can we Substitute a part? Combine it with something? Adapt it from another domain?

name: Reverse Storming
description: Start from the desired end state and work backward to the starting conditions
sample-prompt: In 5 years this is the market leader. Trace back: what had to be true 5 years ago? 2 years ago? Now?

name: Fishbone (Ishikawa)
description: Organize causes into categories (people/process/product/environment) to ensure no angle is missed
sample-prompt: Chart all the ways this could fail. Bucket them by category. Does one bucket have suspiciously few entries?

name: Starbursting
description: Ask reporters' questions (Who/What/When/Where/Why/How) as a framework for exploration
when-to-use: Before launching a product; during discovery
sample-prompt: Who will use this and who won't? When will they abandon it? Where will they expect it to work?

name: Brainwriting
description: Silent written ideation (no discussion) followed by synthesis; avoids groupthink
when-to-use: When dominant voices drown out ideas; neurodivergent-friendly brainstorm
sample-prompt: Write down 5 ideas in silence. Pass it around. Each person adds to or builds on ideas without debate.

name: Rolestorming
description: Adopt a persona (customer/competitor/alien/child) and answer from that perspective
when-to-use: When internal teams lose perspective; innovation workshops
sample-prompt: You are a competitor's product manager. What would you do to destroy our roadmap? Why?

name: Nominal Group Technique
description: Individual ranking + group discussion + re-rank; balances democracy with expertise
when-to-use: Prioritization in large groups; high-stakes decisions
sample-prompt: Everyone ranks these options 1-5. Discuss the outliers. Re-rank. Avoids tyranny of the loudest voice.
